findings.title: The round-up is tested only at 5 items per page, and never with fewer items than one page, so a fix that rounds up by a fixed 4 still passes the suite.
findings.problem: The `per_page - 1` term is exercised only at per_page=5, and no case has fewer items than one page (1 to per_page-1 items, the lone partial page of a short report), so a wrong rounding at another page size goes unnoticed.

evidence.text: tests/test_paginate.py:7, :11, :15 call page_count with per_page 5 only: `page_count(10, 5) == 2`, `page_count(11, 5) == 3`, `page_count(0, 5) == 0`.

With src/textkit/paginate.py:13 replaced by `return (total + 4) // per_page`, the suite reports `7 passed`; that mutant returns page_count(1, 10) == 0 and page_count(3, 2) == 3, against 1 and 2 at the head.
The new test is red on the base commit: with paginate.py at 669de41 the run fails `assert page_count(11, 5) == 3` with `E assert 2 == 3`, so the test does catch the reported bug.

Rerun by the verifier: both mutants of paginate.py:13 (`(total + 4) // per_page` and `total // per_page + (1 if total > per_page and total % per_page else 0)`) leave the suite at `7 passed`; the first gives page_count(1, 10) == 0 and page_count(3, 2) == 3, the second page_count(1, 10) == 0.

findings.proposed_solution: Add, each as its own test beside test_page_count_counts_partial_last_page, a case with fewer items than one page (page_count(1, 10) == 1) and a partial last page at a second page size (page_count(3, 2) == 2).
findings.retest: With paginate.py:13 replaced by `return (total + 4) // per_page`, some page_count test fails; and with it replaced by `return total // per_page + (1 if total > per_page and total % per_page else 0)` (rounds up only after the first full page), some test fails too.

findings.title: Was textkit 0.3.1 published with the rounding-down page_count(), and if so, how will callers that compensated for it learn that the result now changes for every total that is not a multiple of per_page?
findings.problem: textkit is installed with pip and used by the report renderer the README names. A caller that compensated for the old floor, as in the reproducer, now asks for one page past the last, and page() returns [] for it. The version stays 0.3.1 and the repository has no changelog, so only the commit message tells an upgrading user.

reproducer.code:
from textkit.paginate import page_count, page
n, k = 11, 5
pages = page_count(n, k) + (n % k > 0)  # caller's workaround for the old floor
print(pages)               # 0.3.1 (base): 3; head: 4
print(page(list(range(n)), pages, k))  # base: [10]; head: []

evidence.text: Run at base 669de41: page_count(t, 5) for t in (0, 1, 5, 10, 11, 14) gives [0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2]; at head 038a3d5 it gives [0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3].
The docstring at src/textkit/paginate.py:5 promises "the number of pages needed to show ``total`` items", so the new result keeps the documented contract and the old one broke it.
pyproject.toml sets version = "0.3.1" at both base and head; the repository has no tags and no CHANGELOG file; README.md shows `pip install textkit`.
The only caller in the repository is tests/test_paginate.py, so callers outside it, such as the report renderer the README names, are the ones affected.

The repository history has two commits, the base 669de41 being the root that adds page_count with version 0.3.1 already set, so the history cannot show whether 0.3.1 was released with the floor; the author can.

findings.proposed_solution: If 0.3.1 shipped with page_count(), release the fix under a new version whose release notes say that page_count() now rounds up and that callers that added the partial page themselves must stop. If it never shipped, nothing is owed.
findings.retest: Settled by the author's answer: either 0.3.1 was never published with page_count(), or the release that carries this fix has a new version and a note that page_count() now rounds up.
